1 تَنَأَ , aor.
تَنَاَ , inf. n. تُنُوْءٌ, He remained, stayed, dwelt, or abode, (T, S, M, Msb, K,) بِهِ in it, namely, a country, or town, (S, Msb,) or a place; (M;) he settled therein: (Msb:) as also تنا, (M, Msb,) not a dial. var., but formed by substitution [of ا for أ], (M,) [i. e.] by suppression of the ء. (Msb.) ―
-b2- تَنَأَ عَلَى كَذَا He kept, or adhered, to such a thing, inseparably. (TA.) ＝
-A2- Also, inf. n. as above, He was, or became, rich, wealthy, possessed of much property. (Msb.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
